title: os
lede: Node's own lib/os.js, in TypeScript, over the host reads libuv makes: os.cpus() returns live per-core tick counters, os.networkInterfaces() walks the real adapters, os.release()/version() answer what Node answers on the same machine, and a failed call throws Node's ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. os.cpus() speed reports the fixed 2400 MHz libuv nominal on Apple Silicon (where hw.cpufrequency is unavailable), cpufreq's scaling_max_freq or 0 on Linux (VMs and containers have no cpufreq), and Darwin times.irq is 0 — all exactly what real Node reports on that hardware. As in Node, the functions convert to their result: `${os.hostname}` is the host name.

entries.name: os.platform()
entries.description: Returns the operating-system platform string — process.platform, as Node's platform() returns.

entries.name: os.homedir()
entries.description: Returns the current user's home directory, mirroring libuv's uv_os_homedir: a set HOME wins (an empty one included, matching Node's ""); on POSIX an unset HOME falls back to the passwd database, and only a failed lookup throws ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. Windows reads USERPROFILE, else the process token's profile directory.

entries.name: os.tmpdir()
entries.description: Returns the default temporary-file directory: on POSIX the first set, non-empty one of TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP (Node's getTempDir) with one trailing slash stripped, else "/tmp"; on Windows TEMP, TMP, then <SystemRoot|windir>\temp. Never throws.

entries.name: os.hostname()
entries.description: Returns the host name of the operating system (gethostname); a failure throws ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR.

entries.name: os.cpus()
entries.signature: cpus(): { model: string; speed: number; times: { user: number; nice: number; sys: number; idle: number; irq: number } }[]
entries.description: Returns real per-core {model, speed, times: {user, nice, sys, idle, irq}} objects — Linux via /proc/cpuinfo and /proc/stat parsing, Darwin via sysctlbyname and Mach host_processor_info — both verified (on Apple Silicon M4 Pro, model = "Apple M4 Pro" with live tick counters). On Apple Silicon, where hw.cpufrequency is unavailable, speed reports the fixed 2400 MHz nominal that real Node/libuv reports there; on Linux it reflects /proc/cpuinfo's current/scaled cpu MHz, matching real Node. Darwin times.irq is 0, exactly as real Node reports on Darwin.

entries.name: os.totalmem() / os.freemem()
entries.description: Return the total and free system memory in bytes. Verified on Linux and on Apple Silicon M4 Pro — totalmem() matches sysctl hw.memsize, and Darwin freemem() (Mach host_statistics) returns a live free-page figure.

returns.desc: Bytes of total or free memory.

entries.name: os.EOL
entries.description: The operating-system-specific end-of-line marker: "\r\n" on Windows, "\n" on POSIX.

entries.name: os.type() / os.release() / os.version() / os.machine()
entries.signature: type(): string; release(): string; version(): string; machine(): string
entries.description: The uname-shaped identity strings. POSIX reads uname(); Windows reports "Windows_NT", RtlGetVersion's major.minor.build, the registry ProductName with libuv's "Windows 10" → "Windows 11" rewrite for build ≥ 22000, and x86_64/arm64 — verified byte-identical to Node on Windows 11.

entries.name: os.arch() / os.endianness() / os.devNull
entries.description: process.arch; the host's byte order ("LE" or "BE"); and the null device ("\\\\.\\nul" on Windows, "/dev/null" elsewhere).

entries.name: os.uptime() / os.loadavg() / os.availableParallelism()
entries.signature: uptime(): number; loadavg(): number[]; availableParallelism(): number
entries.description: libuv's sources: seconds since boot as a double (CLOCK_BOOTTIME on Linux, kern.boottime on Darwin, GetTickCount64 on Windows); the 1/5/15-minute load averages via getloadavg, [0, 0, 0] on Windows as in Node; the CPUs this process may run on (the affinity set on Linux, the online count elsewhere, GetActiveProcessorCount on Windows), at least 1.

entries.name: os.userInfo()
entries.signature: userInfo(options?: { encoding?: BufferEncoding | 'buffer' }): { uid: number; gid: number; username: string; homedir: string; shell: string | null }
entries.description: The effective user's passwd entry on POSIX (uv_os_get_passwd); on Windows uid and gid are -1, username comes from GetUserNameW, homedir is os.homedir() and shell is null — exactly what Node reports. { encoding: 'buffer' } gives Buffers; a failed lookup throws ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR.
entries.snippet:
const u = os.userInfo();
console.log(u.username, u.homedir === os.homedir());

entries.name: os.networkInterfaces()
entries.description: An object keyed by interface name, each an array of { address, netmask, family, mac, internal, cidr, scopeid } records in libuv's order, with scopeid on IPv6 entries only. getifaddrs (up + running interfaces, MAC from the link-layer entry) on POSIX, GetAdaptersAddresses on Windows; cidr is Node's own getCIDR over the netmask.

entries.name: os.getPriority() / os.setPriority()
entries.signature:
getPriority(pid?: number): number
setPriority(pid: number, priority: number): void
setPriority(priority: number): void
entries.description: A process's scheduling priority (-20 highest to 19 lowest; pid 0 is this process) through getpriority/setpriority — on Windows the priority class, mapped as libuv maps it. Node's argument validation; a failure throws ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR with the failed call's info ({ errno, code, message, syscall }).
differences: The error's `errno`/`syscall` are copies of `info`'s, not accessors over it.
Windows' priority-class mapping is compile-checked only.

entries.name: os.constants
entries.signature: constants: { UV_UDP_REUSEADDR: number; dlopen: {...}; errno: {...}; signals: {...}; priority: {...} }
entries.description: The host's dlopen flags, errno codes, signal numbers and priority levels as null-prototype objects, signals frozen, in Node's own order (node_constants.cc); on Windows errno also carries the WSA* codes.
